newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico overnight Cetes rate pares fall, ends lower.
newsitem.headline: Mexico overnight Cetes rate pares fall, ends lower.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates pared an earlier drop to close down 25 basis points at 22.75 percent on Tuesday as speculators bailed out of paper in late trade, traders said.
"Trade in overnight paper was calm for most of the day, but heated up towards the close," a trader said, pointing out that the average trading rate for the session was lower at about 22.50 percent.
Some dealers who had bought paper early to speculate dumped the paper late in the day.

Traders noted that demand was heaviest for 91- and 182-day Cetes, which closed down 40 and 30 basis points, respectively, at 26.10 percent and 27.20 percent. This was in contrast to what had been a very dull market for term paper in recent sessions.

"Term paper was in demand throughout the session. Foreign investors stepped in to buy across the board in large amounts, apparently to try to force primary rates down," a trader said, referring to this evening's auction.
Light demand for 28-day Cetes in the secondary market reversed earlier expectations that primary rates on this paper would remain stable or rise a little.
A survey conducted by Reuters among ten money market traders showed they expected the bellwether 28-day Cetes rate to fall 22 basis points on average to 23.06 percent from last week's rate.
Overnight rates on bank paper meanwhile closed down 30 basis points at 24 percent.
Total credit maturities for Wednesday were estimated at 5.247 billion pesos.
